title: Explicit local SYN snapshot
description: An immutable imported catalog and its public records. Scope is supplied separately by the Potbot workspace, namespace, and snapshot identity. References carry no global resolver or authority.
$comment: Runtime validation additionally enforces 67,108,864 UTF-8 bytes for both the supplied and canonical snapshot envelopes; 2,000,000 UTF-8 bytes per payload/metadata string; maximum JSON container nesting depth 128 before decoding; nonduplicate references and property names, including same-slug Type aliases across syn:// and synny://; finite bigint cardinality with maximum >= minimum; exact payload id equality and scheme-independent typeRef identity equality; strict embedded JSON parsing with duplicate-key, non-finite-number, and recursive privateData/private_data rejection. contentMediaType/contentSchema describe embedded JSON and are annotations, not a portable substitute for these runtime checks. Catalog merge validates the resulting graph and protects potbot-data- Type slugs under both schemes. No validation step grants authority or performs resolution.

source_label.description: A nonsecret descriptive label. Do not include a database DSN or credentials.

type_ref.description: Exact Type reference under either scheme, with a slug of 1..255 characters. syn://type/<slug> and synny://type/<slug> identify the same Type within a selected catalog. Source spelling is preserved; catalog normalization prefers syn:// for native types and synny:// for protected potbot-data- slugs. Catalog merge rejects snapshot-supplied definitions using a protected slug under either scheme.

object_ref.description: An exact non-Type local reference. The slug is limited to 255 characters for the SQL/HTTP boundary, which is stricter than SYN's general Python ObjectRef constructor.

public_json.description: Exact UTF-8 JSON object text, retained without reserialization. Runtime validation enforces the byte limit and rejects duplicate keys, non-finite constants, and privateData/private_data keys at every object depth.
